chunks: And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'd, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ismail al-Basri, from al-Fadl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered the mosque, and there were some of his companions. He asked them, 'Do you know what your Lord has said?' They replied, 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said, 'Verily, your Lord says: These are the five obligatory prayers. Whoever prays them at their proper times and maintains them, will meet Me on the Day of Resurrection, and there is a covenant with Me for him by which I will admit him to Paradise. And whoever does not pray them at their proper times and does not maintain them, that is up to Me; if I will, I will punish him, and if I will, I will forgive him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the divine promise regarding the five obligatory prayers in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith highlights the theological weight of *Salat al-Waqtiyyah* (prayers at their precise times) as a decisive criterion for the Day of Judgment. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the covenant (*'ahd*) established through consistent observance, while affirming Allah's absolute discretion (*ikhtiyar*) regarding those who neglect it, balancing divine promise with mercy.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 2. And from the previous chain from al-Hussain b. Sa’d from Ibn Abi ’Umayr from Ismail al-Basri from al-Fadhl from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:

“Messenger of Allah (sw) entered the mosque where his companions were gathered. He questioned them, 'Are you familiar with what your Lord has stated?' They replied, 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He then said, 'Verily, your Lord has stated: 'One who offers obligatory prayers five times and that too on prime time, he will come to Me with an assurance on the Day of Judgment and I would make him enter Paradise. And for a person who did not offer prayers on time, I have choice whether to punish him or forgive him’.”'
